newsitem.title: USA: Plains fed cattle trade steady at $72 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains fed cattle trade steady at $72 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold Thursday in light to moderate volume at $72.00 per cwt, unchanged from last week's top price, feedlot sources said.
About 3,500 head traded in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 12,000 in Kansas, but owners weren't knocking each other down trying to sell the cattle, sources said.
"There's plenty who will just wait until next week," one cattle feeder noted.
There also were reports that packers were starting to pull back bids to $71.00 from $72.00, but no sales were expected at that level, sources said.
"They can bid $71.00 all they want, but it doesn't mean they will buy at $71.00," a Kansas feedlot operator said.

Feedlot sources said showlists were not going to be cleaned up this week, but owners could wait until next week to sell cattle, because there were a lot of unfinished or 'green' cattle on lists that could benefit from more days on feed.
